issues.basis: NL2 text; FCSTM transition:line:32 with triggers=[Possible_collision_detected]; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions confirming transition:line:32 source=[*] target=CA scope=llms_emp_feedback_final_0057; exact_source_inventory.transitions tr_0010 (source=@initial:__root__, target=CA, event=Possible collision detected); FCSTM event declarations showing all four collision events as distinct.
issues.expected: The CA sub-machine activation transition must be triggered by Frontend_collision_detected, Rear_end_collision_detected, or Pedestrian_collision_detected (the three specific collision detection events).
issues.observed: The root activation transition (transition:line:32, [*] -> CA) carries a single trigger Possible_collision_detected, which is a distinct generic event not among the three required specific collision detection events.
issues.reason: The NL2 trigger_set contract requires CA activation by the three specific collision detection events. The exact closed-model transition that activates CA (root [*] -> CA, transition:line:32) uses a different single event (Possible_collision_detected). The three specific events (Frontend_collision_detected, Rear_end_collision_detected, Pedestrian_collision_detected) are used internally within CA's sub-composites (FCIdle->FCActive, RCIdle->RCActive, PCIdle->PCActive), not for CA's own activation. This constitutes a trigger_set mismatch on the activation transition.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Possible_collision_detected could be interpreted as a general activation signal that semantically subsumes the three specific collision events, serving as an umbrella trigger for the collision avoidance sub-machine. The three specific events then activate individual controls within CA rather than the CA composite itself.
issues.title: CA activation trigger is a single generic event instead of the three required collision-detection events

issues.basis: NL3 text; FCSTM model text showing CA { Frontend { } RearEnd { } Pedestrian { } UnspecifiedInitial; } without any region separator syntax; canonical_source_ir concurrent_regions count=0; exact_source_inventory.states showing all three composites with parent=CA and no region field; inspection_equivalent_facts.states confirming single-parent containment.
issues.expected: CA must contain orthogonal (concurrent) regions such that Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian can be simultaneously active in separate regions, enabling concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls.
issues.observed: CA contains Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian, and UnspecifiedInitial as direct children in a single implicit region with no region separators. The canonical source IR reports concurrent_regions count=0. In a single-region UML composite, only one child state can be active at a time, preventing concurrent activation of the three collision avoidance controls.
issues.reason: NL3 explicitly requires 'orthogonal regions' in CA to enable concurrent activation of different controls. The FCSTM model shows CA as a single-region composite (no separators in the model text, canonical_source_ir concurrent_regions=0). Without orthogonal region partitioning, the three sub-composites cannot be simultaneously active, directly contradicting the NL3 requirement. No frozen predicate in the registry directly checks region structure/partitioning, so this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate with exact element bindings.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML syntax may not explicitly require separators for concurrent regions in some dialects; the three sub-composites could be intended as concurrent even without explicit region markers. Additionally, the NL phrase 'allow for concurrent activation' could be read as a capability statement rather than a structural requirement for orthogonal regions.
issues.title: CA lacks orthogonal region partitioning; all sub-composites share a single implicit region

issues.basis: FCSTM text: 'state CA { ... [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial; }'; inspection_equivalent_facts: transition:line:30 source=[*] target=UnspecifiedInitial scope=CA, state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:29 has outgoing_transition_refs=[]; verify_facts: 9 refuted reachability checks for all operational states; working_contract: UnspecifiedInitial is compiler_owned synthetic_state; reference_inspection_facts: W_DEADLOCK_LEAF for UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.expected: CA's default initial entry must target an operational sub-composite (Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian) to make the concurrent activation of collision avoidance controls structurally possible.
issues.observed: CA's initial pseudostate edge (transition:line:30, [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial in scope CA) targets a compiler-synthetic state (UnspecifiedInitial, line 29) that has zero outgoing transitions. All three operational sub-composites and their child states are confirmed unreachable from the top-level initial entry by verify_facts.
issues.reason: The derived contract from NL3 requires CA's initial entry to target operational content for concurrent activation to be possible. The exact closed-model fact is that CA's [*] edge (transition:line:30) targets UnspecifiedInitial, a compiler-synthetic leaf with no outgoing transitions, rather than any operational sub-composite. Verify_facts confirm refuted reachability for all nine operational states. No frozen predicate can express 'initial entry must target an operational sub-composite' as a single endpoint pair check (the valid target is a set of three alternatives, not one), hence predicate-null.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: UnspecifiedInitial may be a placeholder that the compiler will resolve to a proper distribution entry once orthogonal regions are defined. The defect might be considered a lowering artifact rather than an author-source structural error. Additionally, the sub-composites each have their own internal initial entries (proven by verify_facts), so they are locally well-formed; only the CA-level entry is broken.
issues.title: CA initial entry targets a compiler-synthetic dead-end rather than any operational sub-composite

issues.basis: NL2 segment; transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-COLLISION-1 (source='unspecified preceding state', three alternatives targeting CA with events frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision detected); FCSTM transition:line:32 (source=[*], target=CA, triggers=[Possible_collision_detected], scope=llms_emp_feedback_final_0057); source_inventory tr_0010 (source=@initial:__root__, target=CA, event='Possible collision detected'); inspection_equivalent_facts showing transition:line:32 as the only root-to-CA edge.
issues.expected: The entry transition to the collision avoidance sub-machine (CA) must be triggered by Frontend_collision_detected, Rear_end_collision_detected, or Pedestrian_collision_detected (any of the three collision detection events).
issues.observed: The single entry transition to CA (transition:line:32) is triggered by Possible_collision_detected, a different event. The three required collision events are consumed internally by sub-state transitions (FCIdle->FCActive, RCIdle->RCActive, PCIdle->PCActive), not at the CA entry level.
issues.reason: The NL2 transition group specifies three collision events as activation triggers for CA. The closed model has exactly one entry to CA (transition:line:32) with a completely different trigger (Possible_collision_detected). The three required events are declared and consumed but at the wrong hierarchy level (sub-state transitions inside CA, not the CA entry itself). This is a trigger_set mismatch on the exact entry transition.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL phrasing 'becomes active when a possible frontend collision... is detected' could be read as describing the internal activation of sub-modes rather than the CA-level entry trigger, in which case Possible_collision_detected at the CA level might be a valid precondition and the three events correctly handle sub-mode activation. However, the NL explicitly says 'this sub-machine becomes active' referring to the whole CA, not its children.
issues.title: CA entry triggered by Possible_collision_detected instead of required collision detection events

issues.basis: NL3 segment; source_inventory transitions showing no CA-level initial (tr_0001 is Frontend-internal, tr_0004 is RearEnd-internal, tr_0007 is Pedestrian-internal, tr_0010 is root-to-CA); FCSTM transition:line:30 (CA scope, source=[*], target=UnspecifiedInitial, triggers=[]); working_contract compiler_owned element compiler:state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0057.CA.UnspecifiedInitial (kind=synthetic_state); PlantUML source confirming no [*] inside CA block; verify_facts initial-entry:transition:line:30 proved (edge exists) but target is non-operational.
issues.expected: CA must have an author-specified initial entry that activates its operational sub-composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian). In orthogonal regions, entry to CA simultaneously enters all regions' initial states. In a single region, at least one operational child must be the initial target.
issues.observed: The source PlantUML has no [*] --> transition inside the CA block. The compiler synthesized transition:line:30 (CA [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial) targeting a synthetic placeholder state with zero outgoing transitions. Upon entering CA, execution is stuck in UnspecifiedInitial and cannot reach any operational sub-composite. The verify_facts confirm initial-entry:transition:line:30 is proved (it exists) but the target is a non-operational synthetic state.
issues.reason: NL3 requires CA to be in an 'active mode' where its regions support concurrent operation. The source has no CA-level initial entry. The compiler inserted a synthetic edge to a dead placeholder (UnspecifiedInitial). This means CA's entry does not activate any operational content. This is a distinct initial_entry property for CA as owner: the required owner-local default entry to operational children is absent. The synthetic target supports the defect but is not itself the locus of violation per compiler-synthetic placeholder protocol.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If CA were properly structured with orthogonal regions (as NL3 requires), the compiler would automatically enter all three regions' initial states upon CA entry, and no explicit CA-level initial would be needed. The broken initial entry is a consequence of the missing region structure rather than an independent author omission. However, even in a single-region interpretation, CA still needs an initial target that is operational.
issues.title: CA has no author-specified initial entry activating its operational sub-composites

issues.basis: NL2 segment; verify_facts refuting reachability:state:Frontend:line:8, reachability:state:RearEnd:line:15, reachability:state:Pedestrian:line:22 (and all 6 leaf states); inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_state_refs=[root, CA, UnspecifiedInitial] only; LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic on state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:29; FCSTM transition:line:30 showing CA initial goes to dead placeholder; source_inventory confirming Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian are CA's direct children.
issues.expected: Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian (and their internal states) must be reachable from the top-level initial configuration for the collision avoidance sub-machine to be operational upon activation.
issues.observed: None of Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian are reachable from the top-level initial entry. The only reachable states are root, CA, and UnspecifiedInitial (the synthetic dead-end). CA's initial entry targets UnspecifiedInitial which has zero outgoing transitions, creating an impassable barrier to all operational content. Verify_facts refute reachability for all 9 states within CA's sub-composites.
issues.reason: NL2 establishes that the sub-machine must be operational (active) upon collision detection. The closed model shows CA's operational content is entirely unreachable: CA's only active substate after entry is UnspecifiedInitial (dead leaf), and no path exists from there to Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian. This is a distinct reachability property: even if the trigger were correct and regions were orthogonal, the current topology prevents any operational state from being reached. G1 checks the representative pair (root to Frontend); the same refutation applies to RearEnd and Pedestrian.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If the root-to-CA transition (triggered by Possible_collision_detected) were to enter CA with proper orthogonal region structure, all three sub-composites would be entered simultaneously via their own internal initial edges, making them reachable. The unreachability is thus a consequence of the missing region structure and broken CA initial rather than an independent topological failure. However, the reachability property itself is independently violated regardless of the cause.
issues.title: CA operational sub-composites unreachable from top-level initial entry

issues.basis: NL2 segment; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers: Frontend_collision_detected (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:12], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]), Rear_end_collision_detected (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]), Pedestrian_collision_detected (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:26], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); verify_facts refuting event-consumer:Frontend_collision_detected, event-consumer:Rear_end_collision_detected, event-consumer:Pedestrian_collision_detected; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostics for all four operational events.
issues.expected: The events Frontend_collision_detected, Rear_end_collision_detected, and Pedestrian_collision_detected must each have at least one reachable consumer transition within CA for the collision avoidance behavior to be operable.
issues.observed: All three events have exactly one declared consumer each (transition:line:12 for Frontend, transition:line:19 for RearEnd, transition:line:26 for Pedestrian), but no consumer is reachable from the top-level initial entry. The inspection_equivalent_facts show reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for all three events. The verify_facts refute all three event-consumer checks. Additionally, Collision_avoided (the deactivation event) also has no reachable consumers (transitions:line:13, 20, 27 all unreachable).
issues.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine to respond to three collision detection events. The closed model declares consumers for all three but none are reachable. Declaration without reachability does not satisfy operational coverage: in any actual execution starting from the initial configuration, these events can never be consumed. This is a distinct event_consumer_coverage property from the state reachability property: even if the states were reachable by some other means, the specific question of whether the events have reachable consumers in the operating scope would need independent verification.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event consumers are correctly declared and would be reachable if CA's initial entry and region structure were fixed. The consumer coverage failure is entirely downstream of the initial_entry and reachability defects. If those are repaired, the events would be consumable. However, event_consumer_coverage is an independently stated property: the current model does not provide operational coverage regardless of the causal chain.
issues.title: No reachable consumers for collision detection events within CA operating scope
